audits.summary: The agent-system half is built and has not changed since commit 24f3002f28 (2026-10-31 20:28Z). It drove six x10 GPU runs with no client errors: campaign 20 smoke and full, the campaign 21 p50 arm, and campaign 23's table_smoke, jit_p50_c44 and jit_p50_c128. Every run used the online table, command keys and explicit ends. The doc's facts hold: tool plus first command word, an entry after 5 gaps, tool and * fallbacks, and about 3 KB with at most 38 entries per request. In table_smoke the engine's own pick matched the client's on all 3,144 turns. The AUC 0.84 and the weak first 15 minutes are x70 offline figures. At x10 the cold start is 29 turns with no entry, all in the first 122 s of every run. Timing differences between arms move the sent p50 by a median 0.04 %. No logged session-end, table or housekeeping item has been fixed; I reproduced five. New: 3 of the 60 tests error against the committed engine. Stale doc statements: the engine 'not committed, not run on a GPU', the hint-free arm 'never run', and 'campaign metrics start at 45 min'. Still open for a real system: an end signal, the real-reply path on a GPU, table persistence, aging and deltas, and a real harness.

clear_conclusions.statement: The agent-side code is complete for the replay and has not changed since it was written. All six dist runs used it without client errors.
clear_conclusions.evidence: git log on agent_cache/scripts/{gap_hints,replay_agentic,reply_keys,test_gap_hints,hint_eval}.py: last change 24f3002f28 (2026-10-31 20:28Z); acceptance notes in results/campaign20/, campaign21/ and campaign23/DECISIONS.md

clear_conclusions.statement: The engine and the agent system agree on keys and gaps. On the GPU, the engine's own pick from the v2 table equalled the client's on every table_smoke turn.
clear_conclusions.evidence: results/campaign23/DECISIONS.md 'table_smoke passed': the key on 3,144 turns, the gap within 1 ms on all 3,034 plans, no plan on 110 turns (81 ends, 29 with no entry). Offline, the parsers agree on 25,617 recorded replies (frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c23_engine/check_reply_key.out).

clear_conclusions.statement: At x10 the online table needs no warm-up period. The weak cold start the doc quotes is an x70 offline figure.
clear_conclusions.evidence: Every completed p50 run had exactly 29 turns with no entry, all sent in the first 122 s (scratch p50_runs.json). x70 offline, first 15 min: 4.5 % of gaps with no entry, AUC 0.618 (online_table_x70.out, 0-900 s row). x10 offline: 1.9 %, AUC 0.749 (online_table_x10.out).

clear_conclusions.statement: Once warm, the table built during a run is nearly as good as one known in advance. It sits low because long gaps join only after they finish.
clear_conclusions.evidence: online_table_x70.out, 2700-end rows: AUC 0.837 against 0.843, loss 0.180 against 0.179, 44.3 % of gaps under the p50 against 48.2 %. online_table_x10.out: AUC 0.692 against 0.673, 44.9 % against 48.0 %.

clear_conclusions.statement: Differences in run timing between arms change the table negligibly.
clear_conclusions.evidence: The sent p50 differs on 43-46 % of shared turns, by a median 0.03-0.04 % (p90 0.34-0.39 %). The picked entry differs on 2 turns, and the p50 crosses the true gap on 0.12-0.18 % of turns (scratch table_drift.py, c21 against c23 at 44 users, c20 against c23 at 128 users).

clear_conclusions.statement: With today's 5 agent systems, the table costs about 3 KB per request.
clear_conclusions.evidence: Rebuilt kv_hints: median 2.9-3.3 KB, max 3.4-3.9 KB, 28-38 entries at the end of a run (scratch p50_runs.json); frozen_reader_check.out: median 3,168 B, max 3,708 B

clear_conclusions.statement: The table's forecast error was the same at both settings and under both routines.
clear_conclusions.evidence: Actual minus predicted arrival: p10 -5.5 s, median -0.3 s, p90 +4.9 s at 44 users, and -5.4, -0.3, +4.9 s at 128 users (results/campaign23/DECISIONS.md). The sent p50 was at or above the true gap on 45.1 % of turns in c20 and 44.7 % in c21 (their DECISIONS.md).

clear_conclusions.statement: At 44 users, the agent side's p50 hints add no measurable TTFT over a hint-free arm with read pins. At 128 users they cost almost no TTFT against exact hints, but lose about half of the new routine's I/O saving.

audits.summary: The evaluation section of DIST_HINT_DESIGN.md stops at campaign 20. Since then the question has been measured at two x10 settings under two routines, and the 2026-11-04 analysis changed what the gain is measured against. At 128 users and 160 GB, the p50 keeps the whole TTFT gain under both routines: +0.09 s and +0.07 s against exact, with within-run intervals that include zero, because TTFT there is GPU queue wait. Under the new routine it keeps only about half of the I/O saving. At 44 users and 70 GB, it keeps 87 % (old routine, +0.46 s) and 78 % (new routine, +1.01 s) of the gain over original HiCache. But a hint-free arm (read pins, paced retries off) ties the old oracle (1.47 vs 1.48 s) and carries 79 % of that gain. p50 hints add nothing measurable over it; exact hints with just-in-time reads add about 0.96 s. So at 44 users the goal is met against original HiCache but not against a hint-free design. At 128 users it is unknown, because campaign 22 never ran. Still untested: x70, methods better than one p50, repeats, and pins versus paced retries. Several lines in the doc are stale, including 'engine not committed, not run on a GPU'.

At 44 users the median wait estimate is 1.0 s against 2.5 s of read time (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:163-164), and the cost does appear there.

Under congestion in campaign 21 it is +0.18 s with an expired plan and +0.77 s without (campaign21/DECISIONS.md:126). In campaign 23, turns forecast to within 1 s (two-thirds of turns) carry 54 % of the gap (forecast_cost_c44.out:14). The cost is shared through host room, eviction and the queue.

audits.summary: Of the long design's stage 1, only part was built: the table intake (the p50 as the point, plus a p50 - p10 early start), just-in-time reads, the arrival gate and the arrival hold. That work is committed (03afa49778, 2026-11-02), and HEAD equals engine_owned_20261101. Campaign 23 ran and evaluated later steps 2 and 3. Lookups that find nothing fall by 90-93 %, the hold is sound, and pins collapse with exact hints. One fetch per reading turn holds only at 128 users with exact hints. Later step 1 is not built: the engine never reads p90, never moves a deadline as idle time passes, and still lets a forecast plan expire into ENDED, which the unit tests assert. Later step 4: landed-span registration and the fix for whole-session eviction are not built. The pin-budget overflow is gone, and host room is now the limit. Under p50 hints, campaign 23 makes three items more urgent: reads sent past the forecast arrival (option A), plan expiry, and the p50 - p10 early start, which the long design had argued against. The QUEUED tier, the cleaner and whole-session eviction never came into play in the 2 h arms. Four things never ran: the restored-KV check, x70, the floor arm and the live reply reader.

Gate plus hold give 0.17 s (4 %) of the 44-user gain, with a within-run CI of +0.03 to +0.41 s (:99, :135-139). Unit tests were not rerun here (host Python lacks msgspec and torch); results/campaign23/DECISIONS.md line 10 records 1,712 passing.
items.notes: One read per reading turn holds only at 128 users with exact hints (1.000). Elsewhere: 1.145 and 1.276 at 44 users, 1.031 at 128 users with p50 (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:173-176). Two differences from §4.7: a re-read is allowed for any reason up to 3 lookups, and the 'covered' rule refuses some reads that would have found data (DECISIONS.md line 192). At 128 users the gate and hold are not separated from read timing.

items.item: Later step 3a: just-in-time staging before arrival
items.section: DIST_HINT_DESIGN.md:138-140; long §4.4 (replaces its fixed 15-s lead); ORACLE_FINDINGS.md §11 item 12, second change
items.evidence: --hicache-storage-next-turn-read-timing just_in_time: next_turn_prefetch.py:832-839, NTP_JIT_MARGIN_S = 1.0 (:97). jit_70 (campaign 24, 75 min) gives -0.85 s, 18 % of the 44-user gain, on 7,410 turns (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:93-99). With exact hints, mean pins fall from 39.3K to 6.2K at 44 users and from 148.8K to 32.9K at 128 users (:66, :83).
items.notes: jit_70 covers only the first heavy stretch. The long design's property that no read goes out before arrival when the queue wait W exceeds the lead (§4.4) was not carried over; see the item on reads sent past the forecast arrival.

items.item: Later step 3b: arrival hold, so reads of queued turns go just in time
items.evidence: read_not_before (next_turn_prefetch.py:914-947) with NTP_HOLD_MARGIN_S = 2.0 (:100); dispatch skips held reads (storage_read_scheduler.py:121-127). Holds per arm: 173, 470, 3,203 and 2,826. None was dispatched after admission and none was left unreleased (results/campaign23/DECISIONS.md lines 56, 104, 140, 177).
items.notes: The hold counts the pages queued ahead of a read, a deliberate change from the design (DECISIONS line 193). At 128 users, reading turns queued 5 s or more are passed by later arrivals 16.7 % of the time with exact hints and 32.1 % with p50, tracking the SSD ceiling (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:196-207). Held reads keep their lookup's anchor lock while parked (median 26.3 s at 128 users with exact hints); this is the logged 'lock nobody budgets for'.

items.item: Later step 3c: which quantile to stage at, and how early to start
items.evidence: One choice was built and run: table plans start p50 - p10 earlier (next_turn_prefetch.py:448, :836; test 'starts early enough for the table's p10', test_next_turn_prefetch.py:924). The long design's §4.1 recommended staging at p50 and argued against p10. At 44 users with p50 hints, staged reads land a median 4.7 s before admission, and 72 % of that comes from the early start. About half of the long pins come from it (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:128-131, 164-165).
items.notes: No arm ran without the early start or with another quantile (option C, not built). DIST_HINT_DESIGN.md never mentions the early start.

items.item: Reads sent before arrival for turns already past their forecast arrival: rule 'read early only if the queue wait cannot cover the read' (option A)
items.section: DIST_HINT_DESIGN.md:183-185 (logged); CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md option A (:234); long §4.4 'W > L gate', §8 stage 2
items.evidence: Not built. At 128 users with p50 hints, 508 of 515 such reads had a wait estimate above read time plus 1 s (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:166-169). These turns' 565 pins hold 37.5K of the 66.4K mean pinned tokens (staged_reads.out).
items.notes: Option A would touch 99 % of these reads at 128 users and 14 % at 44 users. At 128 users TTFT is set by the GPU queue (the forecast costs 0.07 s), so the payoff is I/O, and what that is worth there is unmeasured.

items.item: Later step 4a: landed spans that next-use eviction never registers
items.section: DIST_HINT_DESIGN.md:141; ORACLE_FINDINGS.md §11 item 12 (first change); long §5.2, §7 issue 1, §12.2
items.evidence: _handle_prefetch_result pins inserted_host_node without registering it (unified_radix_cache.py:2459-2462). _on_arrival registers the commit-time tail (next_turn_prefetch.py:581-587). No prefetch_landed_fn exists. next_use_eviction.py is unchanged since f1885117c1 (2026-10-11).
items.notes: With exact hints its cost nearly vanished: 1 turn lost a landed span at 44 users, and there were 0 double reads at 128 users (DECISIONS.md line 55; CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:181). Under p50 hints, 31 turns lost a landed span at 44 users (DECISIONS line 103), and the 129 double reads at 128 users lost their span after the timeout unpinned it. That an unpinned span ranks UNKNOWN comes from reading the code; how many re-reads registration would save is unmeasured. The long design's §12.2 had asked to land this fix with stage 1 for exactly this reason.

items.item: Later step 4b: pins (OF issue 5; issue 12, second and third changes)
items.evidence: The second change (start reads just in time) is built; see later steps 3a and 3b. The third (keep a read parked while the pin budget is full) is not: the dispatch budget is cc.prefetch_capacity_limit, not the pin budget (unified_radix_cache.py:578-584), and pins can still be skipped (:3106-3121). The pin fraction is still 0.3 (agent_cache/scripts/start_server.sh:113), and 'pins only after arrival' is not built. My count of srs_pin_skipped: 0 in every 44-user hinted arm of campaigns 21 and 23, 21 and 27 in campaign 23's 128-user arms, 50 in campaign 20, 98 in campaign 19's oracle arm.
items.notes: The pin-budget overflow of campaigns 18-19 is gone. At 44 users the limit is now host room (about 44K tokens beyond the GPU mirror), and reads are cut or revoked to fit it (unified_radix_cache.py:2976-2987). Under p50 hints mean pins stay at 30.9K and 66.4K.

items.item: Later step 4c: whole-session eviction right after a turn at x10
items.evidence: The code is unchanged: next_use_eviction.py since f1885117c1 and unified_cache/components/full.py since 7f5dd19256. Only a session's newest node is registered (next_turn_prefetch.py:974-996). Last measured in campaign 19 (8,521 planned turns, 35 %). Campaign 20 cites it as why reads come due about 2.1 s after the previous turn (results/campaign20/DECISIONS.md:89-91). Not counted in campaigns 21-24.
items.notes: How large it is under just-in-time reads is unclear. The 2026-11-04 analysis found that the 44-user differences do not come from eviction code (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:124-127).

items.item: v2 table intake and the pick (key, then tool, then '*'), with reply_key_source hint
items.evidence: read_next_turn_table, pick_gap_entry and _resolve_hint (next_turn_prefetch.py:122-175, 423-449). table_smoke matched the client on all 3,144 turns, with gaps within 1 ms on 3,034 plans (results/campaign23/DECISIONS.md line 24). The jit_p50 arms made their own pick on every turn (line 63).
items.notes: A table wins over its v1 companion, and a malformed v2 action falls back to v1 (unit test test_a_table_wins_over_its_v1_companion_and_a_malformed_one_does_not).

items.item: Reading the reply's tool call from the engine's own reply (reply_key_source reply)
items.status: done, not run on a GPU
items.evidence: mem_cache/reply_key.py reads the text form and <tool_call> JSON and returns _no_call when there is no call. An offline check over 25,617 recorded replies printed no mismatch (frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c23_engine/check_reply_key.out). Every GPU arm used --hicache-storage-next-turn-reply-key-source hint (scripts/start_server.sh:173-177).
items.notes: Per-parser native formats are not built (review finding 4). A missing tokenizer gives no key, so the '*' entry (next_turn_prefetch.py:431-432). The cost of decoding at commit is untested.

items.item: Missing-hint and linkage rules; payload bounds
items.evidence: No entry, an ended entry or an entry without p50 all yield no hint, which registers ENDED (next_turn_prefetch.py:376-388, 442-443). GapEntry has no p90, n, max_gap_s cap or max_entries bound (:113-131).
items.notes: Matters only for hint-less or mixed traffic and during the cold start; no arm mixes them. The explicit 'ended' entry (RH (b)) is built.

items.item: One flag --hicache-storage-next-turn-hints {v1,dist} plus a JSON config
items.evidence: Replaced by four flags (reply_key_source, read_timing, arrival_gate, arrival_hold) in arg_groups/fields/memory.py, validated in arg_groups/hicache_hook.py (git show 03afa49778). None of stage_q, dispatch_lead_s, lead_from, pin_before_arrival, missing, late, plan_keep_s, max_gap_s or max_entries exists.
items.notes: Three map directly: arrival_fetch owned/blind is the gate on/off, arrived_hold is the hold on/off, and arrived_margin_s = 2 is NTP_HOLD_MARGIN_S.

items.item: Arrival offset d updated only from exact plans
items.evidence: _on_arrival feeds every plan's offset into the estimate (next_turn_prefetch.py:578-579), keeping values within 0-5 s (next_turn_estimators.py:21). From ntp_plan lines (pred_arr_ms - gap_ms): median d is 0.104 s and 0.117 s in jit_exact_c44 and c128, against 0.441 s and 0.378 s in jit_p50_c44 and c128 (p90 0.88 and 0.76 s, max about 1.9 s).
items.notes: New finding, recorded nowhere. Under p50 hints every predicted arrival shifts about 0.3 s later from forecast error. The effect on results is unmeasured and probably small next to the p50 - p10 early start.

items.item: The read deadline is never 'now' before arrival
items.evidence: read_deadline returns None once predicted_arrival + wait has passed (next_turn_prefetch.py:876-877). That turns a speculative read into a 'now' read, which skips both the read window and the budget (storage_read_scheduler.py:113-135).
items.notes: Bears on reads for turns past their forecast arrival.

items.item: Read-class order: now, then arrived and exact, then speculative
items.evidence: Dispatch orders only by (deadline is not None, deadline) (storage_read_scheduler.py:113-116).
items.notes: It would matter where the SSD runs near its ceiling, as new p50 does at 128 users (1.6-1.77 GB/s against about 1.85; CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:204-207).

items.item: Pins only after arrival (pin_landed_span); release at p90 via finish(ABORT)
items.evidence: Spans are pinned at landing (unified_radix_cache.py:2459-2462). pin_landed_span and staged_read_in_flight do not exist. The only release is at expiry, which waits for an in-flight read (next_turn_prefetch.py:1039-1045).
items.notes: Tied to the ladder and to landed-span registration.

items.item: QUEUED tier, so a queued turn never goes overdue (OF issue 6)
items.evidence: On arrival a plan's next use is set to now (next_turn_prefetch.py:581-587), and the eviction tiers include no QUEUED (next_use_eviction.py:25-29, 82-93). My count of planned turns that waited 60 s or more (ntp_admit wait_ms): 0 in jit_exact_c128 (max 55.3 s), 4 in jit_p50_c128 (max 74.4 s), 51 in campaign 20's 5 h p50 run.
items.notes: Inert in the 2 h arms.

items.item: SSD cleaner deletes by first-write time (OF issue 9)
items.evidence: No 'L3 cleanup' line appears in the server.log of any 2 h arm of campaigns 21 or 23. Campaign 20's 5 h run has two, at 23:13Z and 23:36Z (2.4 h and 2.8 h in).
items.notes: The 2 h arms avoid it. It matters again for runs longer than about 2.4 h, such as a user-count sweep.

items.item: Re-reads through the gate, and the lookup cap
items.evidence: All triggers go through prefetch_from_storage, and the gate caps a turn at 3 lookups and sets refetch_capped (next_turn_prefetch.py:896-900). The cap refused 25 lookups with exact hints and 215 with p50 at 44 users, none at 128 users (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:264). With p50 at 44 users, turns refused by the cap account for 2.15 M recomputed tokens (DECISIONS.md line 89).
items.notes: With p50 hints the cap binds more often than the long design's 'rare'.

items.item: Exactly one fetch per turn also needs host room
items.evidence: _launch_storage_hit cuts a read to the free room or revokes it (unified_radix_cache.py:2976-2987). With exact hints at 44 users, 224 turns needed a second read because the first was cut (results/campaign23/DECISIONS.md line 55). 'Holding a cut read until room appears ... Not built or tested.'
items.notes: A launch asks evict_host for the whole read, not the shortfall (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md small issues).

items.item: Exact and forecast plans follow different rules
items.evidence: In the built engine the difference is concrete: only table plans get early_s = p50 - p10 (next_turn_prefetch.py:448); exact v1 plans get 0. So campaign 23's 1.01 s forecast cost at 44 users mixes forecast error with the early start and with eviction on the forecast.
items.notes: Options B and C in CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md would separate them; neither is built.

items.item: Observability: new and extended events, dist_eval.py
items.evidence: ntp_pick, ntp_gate and ntp_hold are built (next_turn_prefetch.py). ntp_hint, ntp_phase, ntp_landed, nue_evict and the extended fields are not, and agent_cache/scripts/dist_eval.py does not exist.
items.notes: Most of the missing events belong to the unbuilt ladder.

items.item: Calibrated cache simulation to choose stage-1 defaults
items.evidence: Marked 'not started' in the long design (line 566), and no later document picks it up. The CPU model in frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c20_dist/qps_sim.py answers a different question: it picked the 44-user / 70 GB setting.
items.notes: Bypassed: the defaults (1 s and 2 s margins, p50 - p10, 3 lookups) were set by hand and tested on a GPU. Whether the simulation is still wanted is unclear.

items.item: Restored-KV correctness check, and smokes
items.evidence: owned_smoke and table_smoke passed (results/campaign23/DECISIONS.md lines 18-24). The comparison of an SSD-served turn with a fresh prefill has never run (ORACLE_FINDINGS.md:87, 936, 957; no run folder for it).
items.notes: Every result assumes it would pass.

items.item: x70 arms at a loaded point
items.evidence: No x70 run since campaign 18. Campaign 20's x70 section is a calculation, not a run (results/campaign20/DECISIONS.md).
items.notes: Run now, it would mostly measure the expiry rule (long §0, 'What has to come forward').

items.item: x10 arms A0, A3 and A4 of the long design
items.evidence: A1 and A2 ran (campaigns 19-21). A3 and A4 ran only as the new routine without the ladder (jit_p50_*, jit_exact_*). A0 (HINT_SOURCE=none) and A3s never ran (no such config in results/campaign2*/config_*.txt).
items.notes: The hint-free arm, which runs no prefetcher, is a different control.

items.item: The long design's ten open decisions (§12)
items.evidence: Settled in practice: #1 (explicit ends, used in campaign 20) and #4 (new exact reported as the new upper bound in CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS). #9 ran the other way round: x10 first, x70 never. Still open, judging by the code: #2 (prerequisites not landed), #3 (missing hint means ENDED), #5 (the build chose the p10 early start and no late rule, with no recorded decision), #6 (no QUEUED tier), #7 (no inherited registration), #10 (no real end entry; DIST_HINT_DESIGN.md:149-150).
items.notes: No document records a decision on #2, #3, #5, #6, #7 or #10.

clear_conclusions.statement: The brief is out of date: the engine work is committed, not uncommitted. Commit 03afa49778 (2026-11-02 05:22Z) holds the engine files and tests, the working tree is clean, and HEAD matches frozen/engine_owned_20261101 on all 11 engine files compared.
clear_conclusions.evidence: git status --short is empty. git show --stat 03afa49778 lists next_turn_prefetch.py, reply_key.py, storage_read_scheduler.py, unified_radix_cache.py, scheduler.py, arg_groups/* and 5 test files; cmp against the freeze shows no difference. That same commit wrote DIST_HINT_DESIGN.md:83 and CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:249, which both say 'not committed' (git blame). PAPER_PLAN.md:15 still says 'GPU smoke queued'.

clear_conclusions.statement: Stage 1 of the long design was built only in part: the table intake (a p50 point with a p50 - p10 early start), just-in-time reads, the gate and the hold. Not built: the ladder, the late rule that would stop a forecast ending a session, landed-span registration, pinning at arrival, read-class order, the missing-hint rule, payload bounds and the QUEUED tier.
clear_conclusions.evidence: next_turn_prefetch.py:113-119, 376-449, 408, 872-877, 1037-1051; unified_radix_cache.py:2459-2462; storage_read_scheduler.py:113-116; next_use_eviction.py unchanged since 2026-10-11.

clear_conclusions.statement: The gate and the hold behave as designed on a GPU, but 'exactly once' holds in only one of four cases. At 44 users the extra reads come from a lack of host room; at 128 users with p50 hints, from forecast error.
clear_conclusions.evidence: Arrival lookups that found nothing fall 90-93 %. No held read was dispatched after admission or left unreleased. Reads per reading turn: 1.000 (128 users, exact), 1.031 (128, p50), 1.145 (44, exact), 1.276 (44, p50) (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:20-23, 173-183).

clear_conclusions.statement: Just-in-time timing removed the pin overload of ORACLE_FINDINGS issues 5 and 12 for exact hints. The pin budget no longer binds; host room does.
clear_conclusions.evidence: Mean pins fall from 39.3K to 6.2K (44 users) and from 148.8K to 32.9K (128 users). srs_pin_skipped is 0 in every 44-user arm and 21-27 at 128 users, against 98 in campaign 19's oracle arm (server.log counts). jit_70 alone gives 18 % of the 44-user gain, on one 75-minute run.

clear_conclusions.statement: Under p50 hints, what still goes wrong lines up with long-design items that were not built: reads for turns past their forecast arrival (no ladder and no rule that waits when the queue covers the read), plan expiry that releases landed spans and ends sessions (no late rule), and the p50 - p10 early start that the long design's §4.1 and §12.5 argued against.
clear_conclusions.evidence: At 128 users, 463 of 515 pre-arrival reads came due after the forecast arrival had passed, holding 56 % of pinned token-seconds. A plan timeout sits behind all 129 double reads at 128 users and 49 at 44 users (staged_reads.out). At 44 users the early start accounts for 72 % of the early landing and about half of the long pins (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:128-131, 164-169).

clear_conclusions.statement: The long design's warning in §12.2, that a forecast arm without the registration fix would measure that bug, partly came true: the double reads at 128 users lose spans that are unregistered once unpinned.
clear_conclusions.evidence: The code registers only the commit-time tail (next_turn_prefetch.py:581-587; unified_radix_cache.py:2459-2462). Every double read followed a pin release at plan timeout and a span that had left host memory by the time the turn arrived (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:181-183). How many registration would have saved is unmeasured.

clear_conclusions.statement: The arrival-offset estimate absorbs forecast error under p50 hints, which the long design's §3 ruled out.
clear_conclusions.evidence: Median d from ntp_plan lines: 0.10 and 0.12 s with exact hints, against 0.44 and 0.38 s with p50 hints (p90 up to 0.88 s); the estimate is fed by next_turn_prefetch.py:578-579. The effect on results is not measured.

clear_conclusions.statement: The 2 h campaigns never exercised the QUEUED tier, the cleaner or whole-session eviction, so those three items lose urgency for 2 h arms. They come back for 5 h runs or sweeps.
clear_conclusions.evidence: Planned turns waiting 60 s or more: 0 and 4 in campaign 23's 128-user arms (51 in campaign 20's 5 h run). No SSD cleanup line in any 2 h arm. Whole-session eviction has not been counted since campaign 19.

clear_conclusions.statement: Several planned checks never ran: the restored-KV correctness check, x70, the floor arm A0, A3s, and the engine's own reply reader on a live model.
clear_conclusions.evidence: ORACLE_FINDINGS.md:87, 957; no x70 run folder after campaign 18; no HINT_SOURCE=none config; start_server.sh:173-177 always sets reply-key-source hint.

clear_conclusions.statement: Later steps 1 and 3 pay off only if they close part of the 1.01 s gap between p50 and exact hints at 44 users, where p50 now only matches the hint-free arm, or if SSD headroom turns out to matter at 128 users. Whether hints help at all at 128 users is unmeasured, because campaign 22 never ran.
clear_conclusions.evidence: At 44 users: new p50 1.51 s, hint-free 1.47 s, new exact 0.50 s. At 128 users the forecast costs 0.07 s of TTFT and the GPU queue sets TTFT (CAMPAIGN23_FINDINGS.md:11-19, 141-143, 185-189).
